title: Staged compile profiles and runtime dispatch for sparse-routing models
creator: Juniper Lin
description: Objective: Produce a set of publishable compile profiles and a deterministic runtime dispatch policy that optimizes tail latency and cost for sparsely-activated models (MoE with expert gating and GQA variants) while minimizing compile churn and enabling safe version pinning/canarying. This ticket captures the design, on-run experiments, and rollout plan for staged profiles: 1) lightweight warm-start profile for fast onboarding, 2) routing-optimized profile for production steady-state, 3) batch-optimized profile for throughput tenants. The work covers kernel selection heuristics, compile parameter sweeps, KV-cache interaction, cross-shard rendezvous scheduling, and a pinning lifecycle for published profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Three distinct compile profiles produced and stored in the profile registry (warm, routing-optimized, batch)
Automated benchmark harness that compares profiles on representative MoE and GQA model checkpoints with metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU memory, compile time
Runtime dispatch rule implemented and throttled by policy: selection based on (active_sparsity, seq_len, batch_size, expert_count, hardware_tag)
Canary rollout flow that pins 5% of traffic to new profile with automatic rollback on 10% regression in p95 latency or 5% drop in quality (as measured by eval prompts)
Profile metadata (compile flags, kernel choices, quantization-friendly knobs) is recorded and surfaced in the Console per model-version
Zero-downtime fallback: when a requested profile is unavailable, runtime falls back to compatible profile with documented performance delta
implementation_notes: Profile generation: run compiler sweep over exchange: fp16/qat/qat+int8 candidates, block sizes, fused attention variants. Capture compile artifacts and measurement traces for each permutation.
Heuristics: prefer routing-optimized kernels when active_sparsity < 0.3 and expert_count >= 16; favor batch-optimized kernels when batch_size>16 and seq_len<128.
KV-cache interaction: include compile variants that pre-allocate contiguous KV buffers for MoE expert outputs to reduce fragmentation during expert scatter/gather.
Cross-shard strategy: prefer rendezvous kernel variants that overlap communication with compute when model uses synchronous gating; gate async path for high-expert-count to prioritize latency.
Pin lifecycle: publish profile with semver-like tag (profile_vYYYYMMDD-<hash>), create pin window API to bind model:version -> profile_tag, support staged release via rollout percentage and regions.
Safety nets: runtime health checks to detect increased memory OOMs; fallback trigger thresholds and metric-based rollback are required for publish to be promoted to 'stable'.
progress_updates: 2026-03-08: Kickoff meeting with Compiler, Serving, and Evaluations teams. Agreed on three-profile approach and initial metric set.
2026-03-09: Benchmark harness skeleton merged (internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/1481). Can run single-point compile+trace for a small MoE checkpoint.

2026-03-11: Early sweep results: routing-optimized kernels reduced p95 by ~18% on toy-8-expert MoE but increased compile time by ~4x. Decided to keep a lightweight warm profile to avoid long onboarding latency.
2026-03-13: Discovered KV pre-allocation reduces tail latency variability for GQA runs in 75% of traces; added buffer alignment option to profile metadata.
2026-03-14: Implemented runtime dispatch predicate and smoke-tested on dedicated staging cluster. Canary wiring pending console + rollout config UI work.
review_feedback: Design review (2026-03-10): PM asked to include an explicit quality-eval step (eval prompt set) in CI before profile promotion.
Compiler team notes: need to limit compile parameter space to avoid combinatorial explosion; propose prioritized heuristics + cached artifact reuse.
Security team: no additional constraints, but add audit fields to profile metadata (who published, checksum, compile environment).
ServOps: require an ops-visible dashboard for canary traffic and cost delta prior to 'stable' promotion.
